Context: this is a personal dotfiles repo. `tests/ghostty-p10k-prompt.sh` is a bash test harness that copies the user's live generated zsh config into a temp dir, deletes one line from the copy, and renders both variants in a pty via `script -qc 'zsh -i'` to compare terminal escape-sequence output. - Anything that writes outside the temp dir, or that could modify the user's REAL ~/.config/zsh rather than the copy. This matters most: the harness `chmod u+w`s and `sed -i`s files it copied — confirm it can never touch the originals.
- Secrets or identifying data (this repo is public and has a strict no-email-addresses rule) being written into the test, README, or any output the test prints.

Rate every finding Critical, Important, or nit. If you find none, say so explicitly. Report as a list; for each: file, line, severity, one-sentence defect, and a concrete failure scenario (inputs -> bad outcome). Do not propose patches.

    94	render() { # <with|without> <injected|plain>  -> raw pty output, control chars visible
    95	  local v=$1 mode=$2
    96	  # shellcheck disable=SC2054 # the commas are inside one env value, not separators
    97	  local -a e=(GHOSTTY_SHELL_FEATURES=cursor:blink,path,title)
    98	  if [ "$mode" = injected ]; then
    99	    e+=(ZDOTDIR="$GZ" GHOSTTY_ZSH_ZDOTDIR="$D/$v")
   100	  else
   101	    e+=(ZDOTDIR="$D/$v")
   102	  fi
   103	  printf 'true\ncd /tmp\ntrue\nprint hi\ncd -\nexit\n' |
   104	    env "${e[@]}" script -qc 'zsh -i' /dev/null 2>&1 | cat -v
   105	}
   106	
   107	count() { grep -o "$1" | wc -l | tr -d ' '; } # <grep -o pattern>, text on stdin
   108	
   109	n=0
   110	fails=0
   111	ok() {
   112	  n=$((n + 1))
   113	  echo "  ok    $*"
   114	}
   115	bad() {
   116	  n=$((n + 1))
   117	  fails=$((fails + 1))
   118	  echo "  FAIL  $*"
   119	}
   120	
   121	braces() { # <desc> <variant> <mode> <eq0|gt0>
   122	  local out b
   123	  out=$(render "$2" "$3")
   124	  b=$(printf '%s' "$out" | count '}}')
   125	  case "$4" in
   126	  eq0) if [ "$b" -eq 0 ]; then ok "$1"; else bad "$1 (expected no '}}', got $b)"; fi ;;
   127	  gt0) if [ "$b" -gt 0 ]; then ok "$1"; else
   128	    bad "$1 (expected '}}' to appear, got $b -- these cases no longer exercise the bug)"
   129	  fi ;;
   130	  esac
   131	}
   132	
   133	# --- the guard holds ----------------------------------------------------------
   134	braces "injected: no '}}' with the priming" with injected eq0
   135	braces "plain:    no '}}' with the priming" with plain eq0
   136	
   137	# --- the cases above still mean something -------------------------------------
   138	# If either of these goes quiet, upstream changed something and the two cases
   139	# above have stopped testing anything. That is a failure, not a pass.
   140	braces "injected: '}}' returns without the priming" without injected gt0
   141	braces "plain:    '}}' returns without the priming" without plain gt0
   142	
   143	# --- what the priming actually costs: nothing the terminal ever sees ----------
   144	# Skipping the newline pass means the continuation-line mark it splices is never
   145	# spliced. The obvious next thought -- that the mark therefore reaches the
   146	# terminal without the priming, and so the priming trades a real feature away --
   147	# is wrong here, and wrong for the reason the whole workaround exists.
   148	#
   149	# On a p10k PROMPT the splice is what breaks the expansion. mark2 is
   150	# `%{\e]133;A;k=s\a%}`, and its `%}` closes a `${...}` a level early; the OSC
   151	# escape sits inside the expansion that just got cut short, so it is consumed as
   152	# part of the wreckage rather than printed. The `}}` the two cases above assert
   153	# IS that wreckage. The mark cannot both corrupt the prompt and survive it.
   154	#
   155	# So the count is 0 in both variants, and that is the assertion: the priming
   156	# costs no mark, because there was never a mark to lose. Measured as equality
   157	# rather than as "both are 0" so it stays a comparison -- if upstream ever moves
   158	# the splice somewhere that survives a p10k prompt, `without` goes positive,
   159	# `with` stays 0, and this fails rather than quietly agreeing.
   160	#
   161	# `[AP]` because upstream renamed this mark from `133;A;k=s` to `133;P;k=s` in
   162	# PR #11596: on a ghostty that predates the rename it is the A spelling, after it
   163	# the P one, and this case should hold across the bump either way.
   164	mark2_with=$(render with injected | count '133;[AP];k=s')
   165	mark2_without=$(render without injected | count '133;[AP];k=s')
   166	if [ "$mark2_with" = "$mark2_without" ]; then
   167	  ok "injected: priming costs no continuation-line mark (with=$mark2_with without=$mark2_without)"
   168	else
   169	  bad "injected: priming changed the continuation-line mark count (with=$mark2_with without=$mark2_without)"
   170	fi
   171	
   172	# --- nothing else is lost -----------------------------------------------------
   173	# The point of priming the guard rather than dropping ghostty's integration
   174	# (which also silences the `}}`, at the cost of the cursor sequences and half the
   175	# title writes) is that everything else still works. Compare the variants mark
   176	# for mark. `133;A;cl=line` rather than a bare `133;A`: the latter also matches
   177	# the continuation-line mark above on a pre-#11596 ghostty, which made this probe
   178	# read as a regression when it was measuring the intended difference.
   179	inj_with=$(render with injected)
   180	inj_without=$(render without injected)
   181	for probe in '133;A;cl=line' '133;B' '133;C' '133;D' '\^\[\[[0-9] q' '\^\[\]2;' 'file://'; do
   182	  a=$(printf '%s' "$inj_with" | count "$probe")
   183	  b=$(printf '%s' "$inj_without" | count "$probe")
   184	  if [ "$a" = "$b" ]; then
   185	    ok "injected: '$probe' count unchanged by the priming ($a)"
   186	  else
   187	    bad "injected: '$probe' count changed by the priming (with=$a without=$b)"
   188	  fi
   189	done
   190	
   191	echo
   192	if [ "$fails" -eq 0 ]; then
   193	  echo "all $n cases passed"
   194	else
   195	  echo "$fails of $n cases FAILED"
   196	fi
   197	exit $((fails > 0))

escalates zero times.

The `_ghostty_saved_ps1` priming in `zsh.nix` is a model of ghostty's

`ps1_changed` guard fires on the first precmd, which is what stops the PS1

gone with the line and still returns without it, so a workaround that has quietly
stopped working fails out loud, and so does one that has become unnecessary. The
mark ghostty splices to get that `}}` never reaches the terminal either way: the
splice is what cuts the expansion short, so the escape is consumed in the same
wreckage it creates, and the priming costs nothing that was ever rendered.

Hyprland can't enforce: `xwayland.force_zero_scaling` hands X11 clients real
pixels and no DPI hint, and Steam's CEF UI reads neither `Xft.dpi` nor

## Verdict

**No Critical findings. No security vulnerability in the diff.** The specific thing you flagged as mattering most — whether the harness can modify the user's real `~/.config/zsh` — I verified end-to-end and it **cannot**. Details in the "Verified safe" section below.

I found one Important correctness/consistency defect introduced by the diff, one Important pre-existing defect that the diff's own lines depend on, and three nits.

---

## Findings

### 1. `zsh.nix:300` — **Important** (correctness; pre-existing text, but the diff is what makes it wrong)

The diff rewrote the test and README to claim the priming costs *zero* continuation-line marks, but left the authoritative source comment in `zsh.nix` stating the exact opposite — it still reads `one continuation-line mark (`133;A;k=s`, 1 -> 0)`. This is not a pre-existing issue I'm flagging gratuitously: it was *true and consistent* before commit b007ea8 and is *false and contradictory* after it, because the diff changed the claim in two of the three places that carry it.

Failure scenario: a future reader (or agent) opens `zsh.nix` to decide whether the priming line is still worth keeping, reads "this costs you one mark on the first prompt," and weighs a trade-off that the test now asserts does not exist. Conversely, someone reading the new test comment's confident "there was never a mark to lose" and then finding the `1 -> 0` measurement in `zsh.nix` has no way to tell which was measured and which was reasoned. One of the two is an empirical claim someone recorded from a real run; the diff does not say which one it invalidated or why the earlier measurement was wrong.

Note the diff's own commit message ("asserted something that cannot happen") argues from mechanism, not from a new measurement. The old assertion `mark2_without -gt 0` presumably passed at some point, which is where the `1 -> 0` number came from. If it never passed, the README's previous "13 cases" line implies the suite was green with it, which is worth reconciling.

### 2. `tests/ghostty-p10k-prompt.sh:103-104` (inside `render()`) — **Important** (pre-existing; the diff's new lines 164-165 depend on it)

**This is the one real "writes outside the temp dir" finding, and it is pre-existing.** `render()` runs `zsh -i` with `ZDOTDIR` pointed at the temp copy, but `HOME` is left pointing at the real home, and the copied `.zshrc` hardcodes an absolute history path that the harness's two `sed -i` passes do not rewrite:

- live `.zshrc:59`: `HISTFILE="/home/sauyon/.local/share/zsh/history"`
- live `.zshrc:60`: `mkdir -p "$(dirname "$HISTFILE")"`
- live `.zshrc:69`: `SHARE_HISTORY` is set

Failure scenario: running `./tests/ghostty-p10k-prompt.sh` performs 8 `render` calls, each feeding `true / cd /tmp / true / print hi / cd - / exit` into an interactive zsh that appends all of it to the user's **real** shell history — roughly 40 junk entries per test run, plus `SHARE_HISTORY` causing those shells to read and re-import the real history. The same path also reaches `ZSH_CACHE_DIR` writes (`.zshrc:288`, `mise completion zsh >| "$ZSH_CACHE_DIR/completions/_mise"`) and the p10k instant-prompt cache under `~/.cache` (`.zshrc:154-155`). The harness's isolation story is "point ZDOTDIR at a copy," which isolates *config reads* but not *absolute-path writes* the config performs.

This is squarely pre-existing (the `render` function is untouched by b007ea8), but I'm rating it Important rather than nit because the diff's two new lines 164-165 are `render` calls and you asked specifically about writes outside the temp dir.

### 3. `tests/ghostty-p10k-prompt.sh:166` — **nit** (weakened assertion; *not* security-relevant)

You asked whether the change weakened a security-relevant assertion. It did not — this assertion is about terminal escape-sequence parity, not a security control. But it did weaken a *liveness canary*, which is worth naming since the diff's own comment claims the opposite.

The replaced pair contained an implicit self-check: `[ "$mark2_without" -gt 0 ]` could only pass if the pty actually rendered a prompt. The new `[ "$mark2_with" = "$mark2_without" ]` passes vacuously when the harness measures nothing at all, because `count()` returns `0` for empty input (`grep -o` matches nothing, exits 1, `wc -l` prints 0).

Failure scenario: a zsh/ghostty/`script(1)` change makes `render` produce no usable output (integration silently not sourced, `zsh -i` dying early, `script -qc` behavior change). Both counts are `"0"`, `"0" = "0"` is true, and the case reports `ok injected: priming costs no continuation-line mark (with=0 without=0)` — green on a dead measurement. The comment at lines 155-159 asserts this design "fails rather than quietly agreeing," which is true only for the one scenario it names (upstream moving the splice so `without` goes positive) and false for the dead-harness scenario.

Mitigating: cases at lines 140-141 (`braces ... gt0`) are separate renders that *would* fail if nothing rendered, so the suite as a whole retains a canary. That's why this is a nit and not Important.

### 4. `tests/ghostty-p10k-prompt.sh:76,78` — **nit** (pre-existing; sed metacharacter injection via `TMPDIR`)

`$D` is interpolated into the *replacement* half of two `sed -i "s|...|...|"` expressions unescaped. `mktemp -d` honors `TMPDIR`, so `$D` is not fully under the script's control.

Failure scenario: `TMPDIR='/tmp/a|b' ./tests/ghostty-p10k-prompt.sh` → `$D` contains the `|` delimiter → `sed: -e expression #1, char N: unknown option to 's'`, and (with no `set -e`) the script continues with an unrewritten `.zshrc`. A `&` in `TMPDIR` would instead expand to the matched text inside the replacement, silently producing a wrong path. Not exploitable — anyone who controls your `TMPDIR` already controls your environment — and the diff does not touch these lines. Flagging only because you asked about the `sed -i "s|...|...|"` flow specifically.

### 5. `tests/ghostty-p10k-prompt.sh:61` — **nit** (pre-existing; trap coverage)

`trap 'rm -rf "$D"' EXIT` covers normal exit but not `INT`/`TERM`/`HUP`. Bash usually runs the EXIT trap on an untrapped SIGINT, but it will not on SIGKILL or when the terminal goes away mid-`script(1)`. Failure scenario: killing a hung pty render leaves a `0700` temp dir with copies of your zsh config in `/tmp` until reboot. Low impact precisely because the dir is `0700` and contains only a copy of already-world-readable nix-store config.

---

## Verified safe (things you asked about that check out)

**The harness cannot touch the real config.** I traced this concretely rather than taking the comments' word for it:

- The live files are symlinks into the nix store (`/home/sauyon/.config/zsh/.zshrc -> /nix/store/6946i6d...-home-manager-files/.config/zsh/.zshrc`, mode `r--r--r--`). This is the dangerous shape — if the copy stayed a symlink, `chmod u+w` (which follows symlinks) would target the store file.
- Line 71 uses plain `cp` with no `-a`/`-d`/`-P`, so it **dereferences**: `$D/$v/.zshrc` is a fresh regular file with a new inode. `chmod u+w` and `sed -i` therefore act on the copy only. The store originals are unreachable from every write in the script.
- Belt-and-braces: GNU `sed -i` writes a temp file and renames, so it breaks hard links too — even a hypothetical `cp -l` wouldn't propagate.
- `sed -i '/typeset -g _ghostty_saved_ps1/d'` (line 80) targets `"$D/without/.zshrc"` only; there is no code path where `$ZD` appears as a `sed`/`chmod`/`cp` *destination*. `$ZD` is used only in read positions (`-r`, `grep -q`, `cp` source), all quoted.

**Temp dir handling is sound.** `mktemp -d` gives an unpredictable `0700` path; no predictable filenames, no TOCTOU window between creation and use, no symlink-following writes into an attacker-guessable location.

**No quoting/injection break-out for paths with spaces or metacharacters.** `$D`, `$ZD`, `$GZ`, `$HOME` are quoted at every expansion. Critically, line 104's `env "${e[@]}" script -qc 'zsh -i' /dev/null` passes `ZDOTDIR=...` as `env` **argv elements**, not through a shell, and the `-c` payload is the fixed literal `'zsh -i'` with no interpolation — so a `$ZD` containing `; rm -rf ~` or a newline is inert. The only interpolation-into-a-parsed-context in the whole script is the `sed` replacement in finding 4.

**No secrets or identifying data in the diff.** I scanned `git diff 4362f0a..HEAD` for email addresses, the username, and `/home/<user>` paths: zero matches. Both changed hunks contain only prose and escape-sequence literals. The new failure/success messages at lines 167 and 169 print only integer counts (`with=0 without=0`) — no paths, no environment, no render output. The harness never echoes `render` output. Note that the *live* `.zshrc` does contain `/home/sauyon` at line 59, but that file is generated and not in the repo, and nothing in the test prints it.

### 4. `tests/ghostty-p10k-prompt.sh:76,78` — **nit** (pre-existing; sed metacharacter injection via `TMPDIR`)

`$D` is interpolated into the *replacement* half of two `sed -i "s|...|...|"` expressions unescaped. `mktemp -d` honors `TMPDIR`, so `$D` is not fully under the script's control.

Failure scenario: `TMPDIR='/tmp/a|b' ./tests/ghostty-p10k-prompt.sh` → `$D` contains the `|` delimiter → `sed: -e expression #1, char N: unknown option to 's'`, and (with no `set -e`) the script continues with an unrewritten `.zshrc`. A `&` in `TMPDIR` would instead expand to the matched text inside the replacement, silently producing a wrong path. Not exploitable — anyone who controls your `TMPDIR` already controls your environment — and the diff does not touch these lines. Flagging only because you asked about the `sed -i "s|...|...|"` flow specifically.

### 5. `tests/ghostty-p10k-prompt.sh:61` — **nit** (pre-existing; trap coverage)

`trap 'rm -rf "$D"' EXIT` covers normal exit but not `INT`/`TERM`/`HUP`. Bash usually runs the EXIT trap on an untrapped SIGINT, but it will not on SIGKILL or when the terminal goes away mid-`script(1)`. Failure scenario: killing a hung pty render leaves a `0700` temp dir with copies of your zsh config in `/tmp` until reboot. Low impact precisely because the dir is `0700` and contains only a copy of already-world-readable nix-store config.
